governance.note: Inherits the caiso-31 eor-power-hr lever set verbatim (CAMPD net-load-filtered outage windows; EIA-860 cogen-flagged BTM CHP host steam; F923 per-plant delivered gas + measured monthly hub-spot overlay; measured EIA-930 priced interchange / per-hub signed intertie / gas-coupled DSW tranches; measured EIA-930 monthly hydro budget; RA must-offer midday gas floor at the measured EIA-930 NG:NG profile, frac 0.80; Argus coal-cogen BTM holdout; CT_PEAKER temperature hot-limb reliability floor + year-round baseline caiso_ct_floor_base=0.049; the EOR power-only HR correction CAISO_EOR_TOPPING_FACTOR=1.8 on plants 10496/50134/52169; the measured p95 corridor IMPORT deliverability envelope). One new lever, the SYMMETRIC counterpart of the import envelope already in the keeper: a measured p95 corridor EXPORT deliverability ceiling. measured_corridor_flow_envelope(direction='export') returns, per per-hub corridor (WECC_PNW/WECC_DSW) and per (month x hour-of-day), the 95th percentile of measured EIA-930 net EXPORT, applied as the reverse-direction floor of the corridor's interface group (transmission.build_caiso_corridor_flow_groups -> dispatch._build_interface_rows asymmetric 4-tuple). It collapses to ~0 in the evening-ramp (h16-21) buckets where each corridor reliably net-imports, so the LP can no longer wheel cheap CA gas OUT across the seam in the evening peak. This is the exact same class of object as the blessed import ceiling -- a smoothed per-(month,hod) capability percentile the LP clears BELOW, not the hourly residual flow, forward-regenerable and condition-responsive (admissible under CLAUDE.md #11/#12). It is NOT tuned to a TWh residual: it is the p95 of the corridor's own measured export deliverability, the structurally-correct ATC twin of the import derate (import ATC collapses midday under neighbor solar; export ATC collapses evening under neighbor peak).
governance.improvement_note: PROVEN root cause for 2024/2025 and a real structural fix; determination stays NOT-YET (C1 CC_REGULAR still over). DIAGNOSIS (this session, on a faithful caiso-31 reproduction): the handoff's evening-export anomaly REPRODUCES in 2024/2025 but NOT in 2023. In 2024 both per-hub corridors net-EXPORT in the evening ramp (h19 PNW net -0.92 GW, DSW exporting ~1.4 GW) because the export legs keep the full physical TTC and earn the full measured hub spot, so when cheap 2024 gas (HH $2.19 -> CC mc ~$15-20) undercuts the evening hub price the LP runs CC and wheels the surplus out for arbitrage -- over-dispatching CC_REGULAR and inflating the evening LMP. The export cap removes this: 2024 CC_REGULAR 58.65 -> 57.37 (over +4.97 -> +3.55), C3a +48.5% -> +40.6%, C3c >$200 tail 16h -> 2h, evening h19 net interchange -260 MW (net export) -> +1630 MW (net import, correct sign); 2025 CC 58.70 -> 57.73. 2023 is byte-unchanged because 2023 had no evening wheel-out (pricier gas, HH $2.54 -> no arbitrage), so its CC over (+4.73) and tail (621h) are untouched -- 2023's CC-over is a DIFFERENT mechanism (night under-import), not export. RESIDUAL ROOT CAUSE (why C1 does not yet PASS): the remaining evening/night import shortfall is MERIT-limited, not capability-limited -- the corridor import cap is slack in those hours (h19 model import 1.6 GW vs cap 6.4 GW), the cheap CLEAN import tranches (EF=0, hub + small wheel, no CARB carbon) are capacity-maxed, and EVERY further import is priced at the measured WECC hub (~$50, all DSW tranches share the PaloVerde hub) which sits ABOVE cheap CA gas (~$27 with carbon), so CA self-serves the ramp with CC instead of importing. This is the documented static-priced-node tension (IMPORT_TRANCHES['CAISO'] comment: a hub-priced fixed-capacity node trades price-suppression for quantity-correctness). Closing it requires a methodology decision that was deliberately NOT taken unilaterally this session because each candidate touches a guardrail: (a) a sub-hub firm-PNW-hydro economy-energy block exempt from hub-repricing -- most direct but cuts against the keeper's 'price imports at the measured hub' principle and reintroduces (now export-capped) import/export arbitrage; (b) raising the CT_PEAKER local-RA floor toward CAISO's published local-capacity (LA-basin/RMR) requirement -- a double win on C1 (CT into band, must-run CT displaces CC) but the handoff cautions against floor changes and grounding it without pinning-to-actuals is delicate; (c) a steeper CC_REGULAR part-load/marginal offer curve so CA's marginal gas is not too cheap vs imports. REJECTED this session as ineffective (not a guardrail issue): more cheap import CAPACITY -- the DSW tranches all reprice to the same PaloVerde hub so evening DSW import is price-limited (2.1 GW used vs 4.3 GW cap), and clean imports already pay zero CARB carbon (no over-charge bug). The export cap is the structurally-correct fix that stays in (CLAUDE.md #1/#11): it makes the model strictly more faithful (no unphysical evening wheel-out) and sharpens the residual onto the import price-merit, the next session's decision. C2/C5a PASS unchanged.
